Initial IKE_AUTH child is plain (type-6 is CREATE_CHILD-only); the 60s child-SA rekey offers type-06 ADDKE + IKE_FOLLOWUP_KE + ML-KEM keymat, new SPI both netns; kind asserts type-06 offer + the same ML-KEM keymat hash on BOTH sides + no followup abort (not just a new SPI)

PQC CREATE_CHILD response-loss kill-test (review regression): i2ike topology, but netem 80% loss on the responder->initiator veth through the 60s-soft rekey window, so the CREATE_CHILD response is lost on the wire; the initiator retransmits the request and the responder MUST replay the armed response from response_info — gated on the 'R2 replay' marker that ikev2_retransmit_forced() logs exactly at the rate-limited replay; then asserts the rekey still completes with new SPI both sides + type-06 offer + MATCHING ML-KEM keymat sha + no followup abort. No marker => FAIL (a clean rekey where no response was dropped proves nothing); 3 fresh-SA attempts

PQC iked<->iked: initiator IKE_SA rekey (kmp_sa_lifetime_time 30s) offers type-06 ADDKE via WITH_ADDKE; both sides complete SK(1) via IKE_FOLLOWUP_KE and rekey_skeyseed logs the SAME ADDKE SKEYSEED (a plain IKE_SA rekey logs no such line -> fail)

PQC iked<->iked on the INITIAL IKE_SA: SAi1 offers type-06 + N(16438), one IKE_INTERMEDIATE ML-KEM round (RFC 9370 s3.5 SKEYSEED update + RFC 9242 IntAuth into AUTH); kind asserts the SAME intermediate SKEYSEED on BOTH sides + ESP child lands (AUTH+IntAuth verified)

PQC lost-intermediate-response kill-test: netem 80% loss on the responder->initiator veth during the intermediate window (then 5%), which drops a fragment of the fragmented IKE_INTERMEDIATE RESPONSE; the initiator retransmits the gen-0 request and the responder DETECTS it by the cleartext outer msgid/exchange BEFORE SKF decrypt and REPLAYS its cached gen-0 response (`H1 replay` marker — the log line and kind gate). No marker => FAIL (a clean completion where no fragment was dropped does not count as proof; the kind retries establishment with a fresh IKE_SA + flushed xfrm until the replay fires, bounded 4 attempts)

PQC H1 kill-test at REAL 576-MTU fragmentation: veth MTU 576 forces RFC 7383 fragmenting of the IKE_INTERMEDIATE response (ML-KEM KE 1184B); netem 80% responder->initiator drops a fragment; responder must replay cached gen-0 fragment datagrams (H1 replay, fragment count) and the child still lands; i2iinit-drop at veth MTU 1500 proves nothing about the fragment path

PQC R2 kill-test at REAL 576-MTU fragmentation (CREATE_CHILD path): veth MTU 576 fragments the CREATE_CHILD rekey request/response + IKE_FOLLOWUP_KE ML-KEM exchange; netem 30% then 5% on responder->initiator across the 60s-soft rekey (80% blows the 10s ADDKE arm timer before FOLLOWUP install); counted-drop gate (netem-dropped >= 1 AND R2 replay >= 1 AND SKF fragment recv >= 3 AND a new g_ir_present=Y keymat), responder holds its SA (3600s) so only the initiator rekeys; i2iinit-drop576 proves the IKE_INTERMEDIATE fragment path only, not CREATE_CHILD fragment replay

CREATECHILD mid-handler duplicate unit (review #5): netem duplicate 100% on the INITIATOR egress veth after child-up, so the rekey CREATE_CHILD REQUEST arrives twice back-to-back.  Dispatch (ikev2.c:538) short-circuits the second copy BEFORE the handler: pre-arm -> check_message_ordering sees recv_message_id advanced -> dropping-unordered; post-arm -> R2 replay.  Gate: exactly ONE 'CREATE_CHILD_SA request' handler entry (resp log) AND unordered+R2replay >= 1 AND rekey completes (new SPI both sides) AND no abort.  Two handler entries = the window hole is real.  Classical ESP (no ADDKE followup): the reassembler stores SKF fragments unconditionally (ikev2_frag.c:765) with a count-based completion (:778), so a duplicated mid-list fragment livelocks assembly and an ADDKE dup row would fail for the wrong reason.  DPD/NAT-D reply path unreachable (no yield between advance and arm) — documented, not a row.  gate=box: box-only until a container run passes.

PQC REQUEST-direction loss kill-test (review #4): every existing loss row drops responder->initiator only.  This row nets the INITIATOR egress veth (30% until the responder log shows the request arrived, then qdisc removed so FOLLOWUP+response ride the 10s ADDKE arm timer clean); recovery is the INITIATOR's own retransmit ladder (1,2,4,8...s), not a responder replay — no R2 replay expected or required.  Gate: netem-dropped >= 1 on the REQUEST direction AND rekey completes (new SPI both sides) AND type-06 offer + MATCHING ML-KEM keymat sha + no followup timeout.  Completion with zero counted request loss proves nothing.  gate=box: box-only until a container run passes.

veth accounting identity audit (review #2): sent == peer_received + qdisc_dropped on a standalone veth pair, both directions, with netem loss 30% (explicit /dev/udp generator covering UDP/500 AND UDP/4500, kernel ip -s link RX counters, tc -s qdisc dropped; 200-datagram floods, three passes: A->B lossy, B->A lossy, clean).
